To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plan explanations can be understood as a model reconciliation problem (MRP), and that the MRP can be solved efficiently using an algorithm that we call “MRP-Search”.

(1) Explanation can be seen as model reconciliation, (2) Explanation can be used to help humans improve their models, (3) Explanation can be automatically generated by the AI system, and (4) Explanation can be evaluated in a principled manner.
(1) plan explanations are a form of model reconciliation; and (2) the MRP can be solved using algorithms that are based on constraint programming.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) How can we automatically reconcile AI plans and human models? (2) What are the properties of explanations that are useful in such reconciliations? (3) Can we automatically generate explanations that are effective in reconciling AI plans and human mental models?
the question of how to reconcile the AI system’s model with that of the human, and how this model reconciliation can be used to generate explanations.
the problem of providing explanations that are useful to the user in understanding the AI system’s plan, and that are useful to AI systems in understanding the user’s model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is an effective way to explain plans to humans.
this work is a significant step towards understanding how to provide explanations to humans that can be used to improve their models and thereby increase their understanding of the system.
the proposed work would provide a novel and comprehensive framework for studying explanations, and provide algorithms for computing explanations in a principled manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed and developed a new paradigm for plan explanation, which is based on model reconciliation, and have developed a number of algorithms for computing the model-reconciled plan.
we are developing a new theory of plan explanations as model reconciliations, and we will develop algorithms for automatically computing such explanations.

, in this talk, I will present a new perspective on explanation generation, and show how it can be used for a wide range of applications, including human-robot interaction, multi-agent planning, and automated planning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
explanations are not just about providing the AI’s model to humans, but about reconciling the models of AI and human, so that both can work better together.
explanations should be studied in the context of model differences between the human and AI, and that explanations can be seen as an instance of a more general model reconciliation problem.

explanations are not just a way for the AI system to communicate its own model to the user, but also a way for the system to help the human understand the system’s behavior and plans in light of her own model.
